title: "very likely" Means "uncertain"? How LLMs Diverge from Humans in Linguistic Uncertainty Quantification
abstract: arXiv:2610.00083v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Humans express uncertainty verbally via markers (e.g., "possible," "likely"), yet most LLM uncertainty quantification (UQ) relies on costing likelihood- or consistency-based signals. From a cognitive perspective, accurate verbal uncertainty reflects metacognitive monitoring, representing knowledge boundaries ("knowing that you don't know") to support regulation and information seeking. In this paper, we investigate how LLMs diverge from humans in verbal uncertainty quantification and whether verbal markers can reliably quantify LLM uncertainty. We curate a corpus of human uncertainty markers from psychology and decision-science literature and benchmark LLMs against it. We observe that LLMs encode verbal uncertainty with numerical levels that differ substantially from those of humans. We then introduce METHODNAME, a novel optimization-based algorithm that learns an optimal uncertainty profile over uncertainty markers directly from LLM out

translated_title: “非常可能”意味着“不确定”？大语言模型在语言化不确定性量化中与人类的差异
translated_abstract: 人类通过语言标记（如“可能的”、“很可能的”）以言语方式表达不确定性，然而大多数大语言模型（LLM）的不确定性量化（UQ）方法依赖于词元似然或基于一致性的信号。从认知角度来看，准确的语言化不确定性表达反映了元认知监测，代表着知识的边界（“知道自己不知道”），以支持自我调节和信息寻求。在本文中，我们研究了大语言模型在语言化不确定性量化方面与人类的差异，以及语言标记是否能够可靠地量化LLM的不确定性。我们从心理学和决策科学文献中整理了一个人类不确定性标记语料库，并以此对大语言模型进行基准测试。我们观察到，大语言模型为语言化不确定性所编码的数值水平与人类的水平存在显著差异。随后，我们提出了METHODNAME，一种新颖的基于优化的算法，可直接从LLM输出中学习不确定性标记的最优不确定性分布。
tldr: 该研究通过人类不确定性标记语料库发现，大语言模型为“可能的”、“很可能的”等语言化不确定性标记赋予的数值水平与人类存在显著差异，并提出了一种基于优化的新算法，直接从LLM输出中学习最优不确定性分布，使语言标记能够可靠地量化LLM的不确定性。
en_tdlr: This study reveals that LLMs encode verbal uncertainty markers with numerical levels substantially diverging from those of humans, and proposes a novel optimization-based algorithm that learns an optimal uncertainty profile directly from LLM outputs, enabling verbal markers to reliably quantify LLM uncertainty.
